newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast products flat on subdued activity.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast products flat on subdued activity.

text.p: U.S. West Coast product prices remained flat Monday, with trade limited and players awaiting U.S. weekly inventory data, due out Tuesday.
Dealers said the market shrugged off a nearly three-cent fall in September NYMEX gasoline prices.
And cash prices faced increased imports, waning automobile consumption and a low seasonal demand for distillates.
Out West, a lack of concrete refinery news left the market without direction.
"Everyone seems to be running fine," one trader said.

Unocal Corp said the crude processor at its Los Angeles-area refinery resumed service over the weekend. The 125,000 barrel-per-day unit was shut last Thursday for repairs to a pump. Jet fuel in Los Angeles was steady between 71 and 72 cents a gallon, and CARB diesel was the same price in L.A.

Low sulphur diesel, which meets federal rather than California pollution standards, was talked slightly lower from Friday at 68.00/69.00 cents. Conventional-grade gasoline in Los Angeles stayed 65.25/66.25 cents, though one trader assessed it as high as 66/66.50 cents. Premium stayed seven cents higher.
